summary: Remove redundant 'battle involving you' / 'battles involving you' wording from current two-player rules surfaces without changing timing, eligibility, or effects.

changes.subject: Ranger Fieldcraft
changes.before: When a printed Territory effect would affect you, your movement, or a battle involving you, ignore that effect until the end of the turn.
changes.after: When a printed Territory effect would affect you, your movement, or the battle, ignore that effect until the end of the turn.

changes.subject: Inquisition Conviction
changes.before: The first time each turn opposing cards enter the Graveyard during the Aftermath of a battle involving you, gain 1 Conviction.
changes.after: The first time each turn opposing cards enter the Graveyard during the Aftermath, gain 1 Conviction.

changes.subject: Inquisition Condemnation
changes.before: During the Aftermath of battles involving you, opposing Tactics go to their owner's Graveyard instead of their Discard Pile.
changes.after: During the Aftermath, opposing Tactics go to their owner's Graveyard instead of their Discard Pile.

changes.subject: Financier Subsidize
changes.before: Before dice are rolled in a battle involving you, spend Capital to add to your battle total.
changes.after: Before dice are rolled, spend Capital to add to your battle total.

rationale: Gauntlet is a two-player game, so every battle necessarily includes both players. Player-facing rules should state the role, timing, or condition that actually matters instead of restating universal participation.
